Affective Dyna-Q GridWorld Simulator Documentation

Welcome to the Affective Dyna-Q GridWorld Simulator technical documentation. This research framework implements reinforcement learning pathfinding agents combined with the dimensional Valence-Arousal core affect model developed by Johannes Feldmaier and Klaus Diepold (2014).

Project Architecture Overview

  • Maze Generation & Validation: Procedural grid environments generated using Randomized Kruskal’s Algorithm and Cellular Automata. Path viability, start and goal placements are computed via Maximum Geodesic Distance in the largest connected component.

  • Environments: Modular GridWorld environments supporting standard baseline Dyna-Q benchmarks, classic continuous dynamical frequency monitoring (Valence & Arousal), and artificial neural network (ANN) reward-shaping interfaces.

  • Affective Dynamics: Real-time tracking of short-term memory frequencies: collision frequency \(f_{col}\), direction change frequency \(f_{dir}\), goal-in-sight visibility \(f_{goal}\) (via Bresenham line raycasting), and distance-to-origin progression \(f_{right}\).

  • Agent & Policies: Tabular Dyna-Q reinforcement learning integrating direct Q-learning, transition model recording, and simulated experience replay planning.

  • User Interfaces: CLI terminal runner (headless) and interactive Pygame graphical viewer (GUI), featuring automatic publication-ready PNG figure exports per seed.
